exact_statement: For m>=8, d=2^(1-m), L=floor(1/(md)), N=mL, let f be a zero-vertex flip of the product of L m-bit point signs, and a=d-2^(1-N). For every invertible affine physical input change (A,b), the KL of its squared Fourier law to its own actual marginal product is at least N*h2(a)-H(f), with equality in original coordinates. Its minimum over (A,b), even allowing Walsh character phases, divided by ORIGINAL I(f), exceeds (14m-83)/17. The source is full-support and affinely multiplicatively indecomposable, 7/8<I(f)<17/16 and H(f)<69/16. Nevertheless the explicit UNFLIPPED template spectrum Q is full-support and satisfies H(f)+KL(fhat^2||Q)<5*I(f) in the original coordinates. This follows from the general finite-template bound CE(fhat^2,Fhat^2)<=H(F)+2*sqrt(epsilon)*max_S log2(1/Fhat(S)^2), where f,F are Boolean and differ on an epsilon fraction of inputs and F has full Fourier support. No universal FEI claim or bound using transformed I is asserted.
